decisions.executionNote: Approach basket with right arm, raising and pitching gripper downward gradually; keep left arm parked.
Bring open right gripper above the far egg, continuing smooth elbow-up approach.
Align downward gripper over far egg and descend toward grasp height; verify centering before closing.
Close on far egg and lift vertically to check retention, keeping closed target while holding.
First close did not retain the egg. Reopen, correct toward the visible egg center, and lower for a centered grasp.
Lower slightly around the centered far egg, close fully, and lift to verify the egg follows.
Egg appears retained between fingers. Carry it above the holder while keeping gripper fully closed.
Move retained egg toward the holder's far-right cup and begin a controlled descent.
Adjust to an oblique placement approach, retreating wrist slightly to improve reach while keeping the egg over the holder.
Previous action was rejected without motion. Retry oblique approach with half-sized increments for joint continuity.
Egg appears seated in the far-right cup. Open and withdraw upward to confirm placement and clear the holder.
First egg visibly seated. Return open right gripper toward the leftmost remaining basket egg, with clearance above the rim.
Descend open gripper around the leftmost basket egg, finishing downward alignment before grasping.
Close on the centered second egg and lift above basket rim; check retention before transfer.
Second egg follows the gripper. Carry toward the front-right cup with a gentle oblique approach, keeping closed.
Second egg slipped onto the table. Reopen and align vertically above it for a deeper recovery grasp.
Track the rolled egg beside the basket and lower the open gripper to table-level grasp height.
Narrow fingers to clear the basket rim, lower slightly onto the table egg, close and lift cautiously.
Egg remains on the table. Raise and turn open fingers toward a fore-aft grasp to avoid the basket rim.
Finish fore-aft finger alignment and descend toward the table egg, offsetting away from the basket rim.
Replan from interrupted pose: move left and upward clear of rim, finish finger rotation, then lower with reduced opening.
Large residual suggests rim contact. Withdraw straight up with open fingers before moving away from basket.
Approach table egg from above with fingers parallel to basket edge, keeping the grasp center outside the rim.
Lower slowly while shifting slightly away from the basket; inspect whether the fingers clear the rim and surround the table egg.
Center fingers slightly along the egg, descend for a deeper grasp, then close and make a short retention lift.
Recovery grasp was off-center. Reopen and make the tool vertical, aligning over the table egg rather than the rim.
Rim contact prevents descent. Withdraw and angle the gripper from the holder side so the palm stays clear of the basket.
Descend from the clear side toward the table egg with fore-aft fingers, keeping the palm outside the basket.
Fine-center the table egg between fingers, lower to its sides, close fully and test with a short lift.
Continue a slow vertical lift with the gripper closed to verify whether the recovered egg is retained.
Egg did not follow. Reopen and correct grasp center toward its visible position, approaching more deeply with fingers along the rim.
Egg is now visually centered between open fingers. Close at the observed pose and lift straight up to test retention.
Table egg remains blocked by the rim. Clear upward and approach the accessible front basket egg first.
Align vertically over the front basket egg and lower open fingers around it, preserving elbow-up posture.
Lower slightly around the centered front egg, close fully, then make a short vertical retention lift.
Front egg moved rather than lifting. Reopen, follow its new position, and lower further so fingers reach its sides.
Bring the fingers toward the front egg seen below the jaw tips, maintaining height and a moderate opening to avoid the rim.
Egg now appears centered at the jaw tips. Close fully at this pose and lift slowly without changing orientation.
Front egg appears retained. Carry slowly toward the empty front-right cup while preserving grasp orientation and full closure.
Lower retained egg toward the front-right cup, keeping the grasp orientation fixed to minimize slipping.
Set the retained egg into the front-right cup, open fingers, and withdraw upward to inspect the placement.
Two eggs are visible in the holder. Move the open right gripper above the last egg still in the basket.
Center above the remaining basket egg and descend gradually with open fingers.
Fine-center on the egg, close the jaws and lift slowly to check retention before transporting.
Egg appears retained. Lift above the rim and begin a slow transfer without changing the grasp orientation.
Carry the retained egg toward the far-left empty cup; tilt gently so the right wrist stays in its workspace.
Lower the retained egg toward the far-left cup while keeping the right wrist on the right side and the gripper closed.
Lid contact caused substantial tracking error and the egg appears released near the left cup. Open and withdraw upward/away to inspect seating.
No motion executed after continuity rejection. Re-anchor at observed pose and withdraw in smaller increments with fingers open.
Three eggs are visibly seated. Clear the lid and orient for a fore-aft grasp of the remaining table egg, with palm outside the basket.
Finish turning fingers parallel to the basket edge while lowering toward the remaining table egg.
The basket rim obstructs the table egg. Move to a clear section of the empty basket to shift it aside before recovering the egg.
Gently test whether the empty basket can shift right at a clear rim section, away from the remaining egg.
Basket did not shift. Approach with narrow closed fingers between the rim and table egg to gently move the egg into clearer space.
Move the narrow fingers left away from the rim, attempting to nudge the egg into the open gap beside the holder.
Rim blocks lateral motion. Open and lift vertically to clear it, then move outside the basket for a fresh approach.
Approach the table egg from the holder side, angling the fingers inward while keeping the wrist clear of the basket.
Side approach is obstructed. Re-anchor and withdraw toward the front to clear both basket and holder before changing the approach angle.
Retry continuity alignment with a minimal initial adjustment, then withdraw upward and toward the front.
Reorient in free space for an angled approach from the front, keeping the wrist away from both containers.
Lower from the front with an oblique gripper, keeping the palm behind the egg and reducing opening to clear nearby obstacles.
Test the front-side grasp at this lower position, then lift slowly with the gripper closed to check for retention.
Grasp retention remains unclear. Reopen and retreat upward toward the front to expose the remaining egg and avoid the basket rim.
Reorient above obstacles for a fore-aft grasp, approaching from the holder side with the wrist left of the egg.
Finish the inward-tilted fore-aft orientation above the table egg, staying clear of the basket while approaching.
Move farther outside the rim while descending, using the wrist view to bring the table egg between the fingers.
Replan after contact interruption. Withdraw toward the front and rotate above the obstacles for another angled grasp; verify by carrying before opening.
Retry with a tiny initial continuity correction; no prior motion executed. Then clear upward and toward the front.
Finish the front-side oblique approach with fingers open, descending without reaching across either arm.
Approach the table egg more deeply from the front, shifting slightly outside the basket and keeping moderate finger clearance.
Front-side fingers remain obstructed by the rim. Clear upward and begin a stronger inward-angled side approach with fore-aft fingers.
Replan after interruption: first clear straight upward from the observed pose without rotating against the rim.
No movement on rejection. Use a modest correction toward the preceding accepted target to bridge continuity, then lift straight clear.
In free space, shift the wrist toward the holder side and begin a stronger inward tilt with fore-aft fingers so the palm can clear the rim.
Continue the stronger inward tilt and fore-aft finger alignment above the egg, lowering only while clear of the holder and rim.
Lower with a stronger inward tilt and fore-aft jaws, aiming at the egg while keeping the wrist outside the basket rim.
